problem: The term 'hot spot' is used without explanation, and a first-time reader may confuse it with a Wi-Fi hot spot.
fix: Add: 'A hot spot is an invisible clickable region drawn over part of the card; clicking it follows its link.'

problem: 'Keyframe marks a change' is thin. Between two keyframes the tool calculates the in-between values, which is the whole reason keyframes are powerful; without that, a student reads keyframes as just bookmarks.
fix: Say: 'A keyframe is a frame where the author fixes an object's value, for example its position or opacity. Between two keyframes the tool fills in the values, called tweening, so a caption can fade in from 18.5 s to 20.0 s without the author setting every frame.'

problem: 'Instances' is used in 'all its instances update' but never defined; the cast/instance pair is the key idea of this metaphor.
fix: Define it where it first appears: 'An instance is one placement of a cast member on the timeline. Many instances can point to the same cast member, so editing the cast member changes every instance.'

problem: 'Interactivity is expressed as control flow between icons, not as a button on a page' is too absolute. Icon tools also let an icon contain clickable buttons and hot spots that branch; the difference is that the branch is drawn in the flow, not that buttons are impossible.
fix: Write: 'Interactivity is mainly expressed as control flow between icons rather than as a button on a page; a button inside an icon still leads to a link drawn as a flowline.'
